name: Besodeiah
overview: Besodeiah is a male biblical figure known primarily as the father of Meshullam, as recorded in Nehemiah 3:6. There is no recorded tribal affiliation or additional personal details beyond this familial connection. His brief mention suggests a role within the post-exilic community involved in the rebuilding efforts of Jerusalem.
namesAndTitles: The name Besodeiah means 'in secret council of YHWH,' reflecting a possible spiritual significance or divine guidance associated with his identity. This proper name, as given in Nehemiah 3:6, is not indicated to have been divinely assigned but carries a meaningful Hebrew expression.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Besodeiah as the father of Meshullam, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, no other family relationships are recorded or inferred in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Besodeiah's significance lies in his connection to Meshullam, who is noted in the context of the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls. This association places Besodeiah within the community committed to restoring the city under God's providence after the exile. Although his mention is brief, it situates him within the covenant people actively participating in God's redemptive plan during this period.
